newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to edge up but resistance secure.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to edge up but resistance secure.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold prices could creep back over $343.00 per ounce on Thursday after coming under pressure from a stronger dollar overnight, technical analysts said.
However, resistance at $346.50 was unlikely to be troubled even if additional support was gained from a rebounding platinum price, they added.
GOLD -
Good physical demand for gold should ensure prices climb back to around $343.00 on Thursday but much will depend on the dollar's moves on the foreign exchange markets, analysts said.
The dollar leapt to over 115 yen overnight but by early in the Europe trading day it was in the middle of its trading range as its bounce lost momentum.
Even so Tocom gold went the 40-yen limit up when the dollar surge was at its peak.
"Gold could go slightly higher today due to physical demand. There is not much movement though and it will stay in a tight range," a technical analyst said.
The 10- and 30-day moving averages converging around $343.50 provided an interim target for the market but the breakout points at $345.50 and $346.50 were unlikely to be troubled.
On the downside, a base looks close to confirmation at $340.00-$337.00, they said.
At 0710 GMT gold was indicated at $342.15/$342.55, down from Wednesday's $343.80/$344.30 close.
SILVER -
There was little movement in silver early in Europe and scant prospect of a move away from the middle of its $4.70-$4.90 trading range, analysts said.
Last week's failure at $4.95 has left dealers a little wary, even though firmness within the range is favoured, they said.
"It has tested both ends of the range several times and doesn't seem to have the momentum to break through in either direction," an analyst said.
The 10-and 30-day moving averages have aligned on $4.76, suggesting support for a step-up move is possible.
At 0710 GMT, silver was indicated at $4.75/$4.77, a cent under the Wednesday close.
PLATINUM -

The heat has gone out of platinum and palladium but the markets will still be prone to reactions on any suggestion of postponements to Russia's long-delayed 1997 export campaign start-up, analyst said.
"There is still a lot of volatility in the market, albeit that it is losing momentum," one analyst said.
Platinum can expect support at $440.00, but with spreads down to $5.00 from $30.00 last week, it would take a significant scare to re-test last Friday's $505 high.
At 0710 GMT platinum was indicated at $446.00/$451.00, down $9.00 from Wednesday's London close.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
